Short Wave podcast: Revealing the science behind everyday mysteries

Short Wave

Want a better winter workout? Train your muscle clocks

TikTok has another trend: the winter arc. It's a self-improvement challenge where people try to be their best self in the 3 months leading up to New Year – often, through exercise. We at Short Wave wanted to know if the science really holds up: Is ramping up your exercise routine when your circadian rhythm may be struggling with less light really a good idea? So we called up NPR health correspondent, Will Stone. He's done a deep dive on what scientists do and don't know about exercise and our circadian rhythms.To read more of Will's reporting on creating a solid exercise routine.If you liked this episode, check out our episodes on "circadian depression", and the science of jet lag and how to avoid it. How to make the juiciest, tastiest Thanksgiving turkey, according to science

Turkey is the usual centerpiece of the Thanksgiving dinner, but it's all too easy to end up with a dry, tough, flavorless bird. For NPR science correspondent Maria Godoy, it got so bad that several years ago, her family decided to abandon the turkey tradition altogether. Can science help her make a better bird this year? That's what she hopes as she seeks expert advice from food science writers and cookbook authors Nik Sharma and Kenji López-Alt. Want to know what other delectable food secrets science has to offer? Email shortwave@npr.org and we just might find out for you!

Short Wave

Here are science-backed tips on how to navigate holiday arguments

Many people are gearing up for holiday conversations with loved ones who may disagree with them — on everything from politics to religion and lifestyle choices. As the conversations unfold, these divisions are visible in our brains too. These conversations can get personal and come to a halt fast. But today on the show we get into research in neuroscience and psychology showing that as much as we disagree, there are ways to bridge these divides – and people who are actively using these strategies in their daily lives. Want to hear more neuroscience and psychology? Wild turkeys almost went extinct. Now they're in trouble again

As a teen, Mike Chamberlain spent all his free time hunting turkeys. Now, his job is researching everything about them – the birds' behavior, their genetics and more. And for the past decade, he's focused on their concerning decline in the American southeast. Today on the show, Emily chats with Mike about what could be driving the loss of turkey territory – and what conservationists – including hunters – are doing about it. How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region

100 Years of Kicks on Route 66

Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one

Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Oklahoma, was Route 66's first Black-owned gas station. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, and use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.
